title: Hearty Light Portuguese Black Bean Stew
description: A crowd-pleasing and light Portuguese dish featuring fermented black beans, this stew is a bitter and savory delight. It is prepared using a bain-marie and served in a bamboo tray, making it a perfect option for a Buddhist temple gathering.
instructions: In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat using a bain-marie.
Add the chopped onion and cook until it is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add the fermented black beans, water, salt, black pepper, and bay leaves to the pot.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves and stir in the chopped parsley.
Serve the stew hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired, in a bamboo tray.
Let it cool for a few minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
